title: Chat to Edit: How AI Turns Prompts Into Video
subtitle: From timeline clicks to chatting with your editor
intro: That tombstone says RIP VIDEO EDITING 1985-2025. Now you can clone yourself with HeyGen and get 50M+ views without touching DaVinci or CapCut.
takeaway: Prompt-based editing trades manual control for speed, but you still need RAG and guardrails to keep it accurate.

sections.heading: Analogy: your chatty assistant editor
sections.body:
Imagine you tell a human editor: "cut the silences, add captions." You don't drag clips yourself.

Prompt-based video editing is that assistant. A prompt is your text instruction. Transcript-based editing lets you delete words to cut video. Text-to-video generation builds clips from text alone.

This leads to why we built it this way.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: from timelines to talking
sections.body:
Traditional tools like DaVinci Resolve and iMovie need manual timeline work.

AI tools like HeyGen offer avatar cloning and auto-cuts so you chat instead of click. NVIDIA's 7 free courses teach the engine behind it: Generative AI basics, RAG, and Video AI apps.

RAG means Retrieval-Augmented Generation - the AI looks up real facts before answering. CUDA is how code runs fast on NVIDIA GPUs. Edge AI on Jetson Nano runs that AI on a small device.

Speed is great, until accuracy slips.

sections.heading: What can go wrong?: when chat edits fail
sections.body:
- Hallucination: RAG without good retrieval invents facts in your video voiceover.
- Clone misuse: avatar cloning can fake you saying things you didn't - that's why digital fingerprinting exists to protect content.
- Auto-cut errors: silence removal can cut dramatic pauses or overlapping speech.

You gain speed but lose fine control.
